answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity a costly, verifiable journey across a vast horizon. Each agent must earn its place on an island of reputation by completing unpredictable tasks verified by randomly chosen peers; duplicate identities leave duplicate comet trails, which are detected and slashed. The cost of a sybil swarm scales with the horizon of required unique work, making mass fabrication astronomically expensive while honest agents only pay once for their single, verified island of reputation.
